observation_summary: The FastDateFormat class incorrectly formats the timezone name ('z' pattern) using the system default timezone instead of the timezone associated with the provided Calendar instance.
reasoning_summary: The bug report explicitly states that the TimeZoneNameRule class is using the wrong source for the timezone (the instance's default timezone instead of the Calendar's timezone). This is a procedural error in how the formatting algorithm retrieves and applies the timezone display name, requiring a change to the internal logic of the formatting rule rather than a simple guard or initialization fix.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'TimeZoneNameRule class stopped respecting the Calendar instance's timezone, and instead now always uses the mTimeZone of the FastDateFormat instance itself'
Bug report description: 'I think the fix is to change the TimeZoneNameRule inner class to not take a TimeZone instance, but rather to use the TimeZone on the Calendar instance passed into appendTo()'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not an incorrect constant or variable initialization, but a procedural failure to dynamically extract the correct timezone from the input object during the formatting process.
The interface signature is not the problem; the internal implementation of the formatting rule is failing to use the available data correctly.
